Background | Information

Background Information | Expressions | are | a | form | of | external | expression | of | human | emotions | . | There | are | three | main | ways | of | human | expression | : | facial | expression, | language | tone | expression, | and | body | posture | expression | .

Background Information | Facial | expression | refers | to | the | expression | of | various | emotional | states | through | the | changes | in | eye | muscles, | facial | muscles, | and | oral | muscles | . | For | example, | eyes | can | not | only | express | feelings | but | also | communicate | ideas, | and | facial | expressions | are | a | very | important | means | of | non | - | verbal | communication | . | Artists | often | express | the | inner | emotions | and | emotions | of | the | characters | through | the | depiction | of | the | facial | expressions | of | the | characters | and | vividly | show | the | spiritual | outlook | of | the | characters | .

Background Information | Facial | expressions | serve | as | a | powerful | tool | for | communication | . | A | fascinating | demonstration | of | this | is | through | imitation | . | Humans | and | orangutans | alike | often | physically | mimic | the | emotions | of | those | around | them | . | When | individuals | sense | another's | sadness, | they | naturally | display | sadness | themselves | - | as | Darwin | once | observed | . | This | imitation | is | likely | an | effort | to | express | sympathy | and | shared | sorrow | in | response | to | difficult | experiences | .

Background Information | Facial | expressions | can | be | divided | into | eight | categories | : | excitement, | joy, | surprise, | sadness, | fear, | shyness, | contempt | or | disgust, | and | anger | . | In | general, | the | muscle | groups | around | the | eyes | and | mouth | are | the | most | expressive | parts | of | the | face | .
Knowledge  | Introduction

Knowledge Introduction | Clowns | are | comedians | with | the | most | facial | expressions | . | They | often | perform | on | stages, | circuses, | variety | shows, | carnivals, | children's | shows | and | birthday | parties | . | In | order | to | let | everyone | feel | the | emotions | of | the | characters | as | much | as | possible, | they | tend | to | exaggerate | all | expressions | . | Therefore, | actors | who | play | clowns | need | to | have | a | very | deep | understanding | of | different | expressions | .

Knowledge Introduction | When | clowns | perform, | they | often | wear | oversized | shoes | and | exotic | clothes | . | Their | faces | are | also | painted, | especially | the | nose | . | These | wacky, | hilarious | costumes | bring | laughter | to | the | audience | . | Usually, | clowns | entertain | audiences | by | embarrassing | themselves | . | Today, | we | will | use | the | dot | matrix | screen | to | make | the | eyes | of | the | clown | and | make | different | expressions | through | different | eyes | .

Dot Matrix Screen | The | 16 | x | 16 | dot | matrix | screen | is | an | electronic | component | that | can | be | used | to | display | Chinese | characters, | letters, | numbers | and | expressions | . | A | variety | of | functions | can | be | realized, | including | 16 | - | level | brightness | adjustment, | customizing | the | on | and | off | of | each | point, | scrolling | display | strings, | displaying | hand | - | drawn | expressions, | etc | .

Programming Module | Show Pattern | Make the dot matrix screen display the specified pattern. | Parameter value: 1 | - | 8, connection port | Parameter value: 4*16 | - | bit "0000" data, each 4 | - | bit data represents a row of dot  | matrix data, calculated in hexadecimal. | Parameter value: 0 | - | 15, 16 levels of controllable brightness adjustment

Practice | Flow Chart | Press | the | button | and | release | it | to | switch | between | different | eye | shapes | . | Then, | the | variable | will | continue | to | increase, | but | the | number | of | expressions | is | limited | . | When | the | variable | value | exceeds | the | number | of | expressions, | the | expression | will | no | longer | change | . | In | switching | expressions, | you | need | to | use | a | remainder | algorithm | .
